html:
The Toromona are an uncontacted Indigenous people of north-western Bolivia, believed to live near the upper Madidi and Heath rivers, on the forested slopes where the Andes drop into the Amazon. They are thought to speak a Tacanan language, related to that of the Tacana and the Ese Ejja.

Explorers and missionaries mention them from colonial times, and the rubber boom of the late 1800s brought violence to the region. Since then they have avoided outsiders, and there is no confirmed recent contact. In 2006 Bolivia set aside an "exclusive, reserved and inviolable" zone inside Madidi National Park to protect them, one of the few such reserves for uncontacted peoples in South America.
